newsitem.title: GERMANY: Canadian canola trades in N.Europe rapeseed market.
newsitem.headline: Canadian canola trades in N.Europe rapeseed market.

text.p: Canadian canola traded at $350 a tonne in northern Europe where supply from sharply lower domestic rapeseed crops was limited, brokers said.
Domestic volumes brought to the market were snapped up by trade buyers while crushers declined to compete for the material as returns from product sales were unsatisfactory.
"Harvesting in northern Germany is about to be completed and supply is well down. Prices should stay firm, especially with Scandinavian and Polish buyers lining up," one broker said.
Buyers free Hamburg offered 465 marks/tonne, 7.50 marks more than last week and 25 marks more than in late July.
Northern and eastern European crops suffered winter damage and the EU crop is seen falling to 6.9 million tonnes from last year's 8.2 million, analysts say.
Price support also came from a higher Chicago soycomplex which rose on Chinese bean buying talk and dry U.S. weather.
Demand for soft oils and meals in Europe was subdued.

Rapeseed buyers at points other than Hamburg offered up to 10 marks more for September than last week, with bids in a 450-460 marks range, but Dutch buyers reduced their bids amid Canadian import pressure.
The November position on the Paris Matif futures exchange last traded three marks above last night's close at 467 marks.

Local rape meal sellers quoted September/October meal (34 percent protein) at 28.25-28.50 marks/100 kg, up from 27.50-27.75 marks last week, while November/January was down 0.50 on the week at 28.25 marks.
By comparison, spot soymeal cost 43.25-43.50 marks (44 percent protein).
September rape oil was at 86.00 marks and October at 86.25 marks versus 85.50 marks asked last week for both September and October.
November/January oil was at 88.25 marks, up 0.50.
